'''''Culcita macrocarpa''''', the '''woolly tree fern''', is a species of [[fern]] in the family [[Culcitaceae]] native to [[Macaronesia]] and parts of the [[Iberian Peninsula]],<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /> where it might have been [[introduced species|introduced]]. It is the only member of the order [[Cyatheales]] that is native to Europe.

==Description==
''Culcita macrocarpa'' is a large [[plant]] that can reach up to {{convert|2|m|ft}} in height<ref>{{cite web |title=Cucita macrocarpa |url=http://islandlab.uac.pt/fotos/publicacoes/publicacoes_Culcita_macrocarpa_EspeciesDirectivaAvesHabitatsAnexoII.pdf |publisher=islandlab.uac.pt/ |access-date=8 December 2020}}</ref> and has [[fronds]] up to {{convert|2|m|ft}} long. Its [[rhizome]]s are thickly coated with long silky, light brown hairs. [[Stipe (botany)|Stipes]] are one third of the [[leaf|blade]] length, it has glabrous stabs and [[rachis]] and a shiny green, leathery, triangular blade on top. Serums are protected by the blade's curved lobes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Culcita macrocarpa C. Presl |url=http://www3.uma.pt/biopolis/planta.php?id=217 |publisher=[[University of Madeira]] |access-date=8 December 2020}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
[[File:Culcita macrocarpa (15697203838).jpg|thumb|left|''Culcita macrocarpa'' stipes]]
''Culcita macrocarpa'' is [[endemic]] to [[Portugal]] and [[Spain]], both on the [[Iberian Peninsula]] and [[Macaronesia]]. It can be found in all of the [[Azores]] islands except [[Graciosa]], in the [[Madeira Island|Island of Madeira]] part of the [[Madeira|Madeira Archipelago]] and in [[Tenerife]] on the [[Canary Islands]]. It is very rare in [[Santa Maria Island|Santa Maria]]. In the Iberian Peninsula it is found in the north [[Cantabria]]n and [[Asturias|Asturian]] coasts, northern [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]] and in mountainous areas around [[Porto metropolitan area|Porto]] and the [[Province of Cádiz]].<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /> The populations found in Iberia might be the result of an [[introduced species|introduction]].<ref name="flora-on">{{cite web |title=Culcita macrocarpa C.Presl |url=https://flora-on.pt/#/1culcita+macrocarpa |publisher=[[Flora-On]] |access-date=23 August 2021}}</ref>

It grows on siliceous rocky slopes, especially in deep valleys under evergreen forest and near coastal areas, sometimes in scrubland up to {{convert|1100|m|ft}} elevation. It is usually found close to waterfalls or streams that provide moisture in the form of spray. This species requires shade and warm temperatures all year round, with high atmospheric humidity to flourish.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" />

It grows in all types of soils but avoids limestone substrates and is especially common on the herbaceous layer of high elevation montane forests of the Azores.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" />

==Threats==
''Culcita macrocarpa'' is threatened by the conversion of forests into plantations. In [[mainland Portugal]], where it is classified as [[critically endangered]],<ref name="flora-on" /> [[Wildfire|fire]] is the main threat to the species and [[eucalyptus]] plantations cause soil desiccation that prevent the species from growing.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" />
